messages.content: deeptraffic-compact-prompt-v6. Control one car on a seven-lane highway and maximize average fleet speed. The user supplies an observation summary plus native engine lane-change status. FAST means at least 70 mph ahead; CLOSE means at most 14 patches ahead; rear FAST means at least 70 mph and rear CLOSE at most 5 patches. SLOW is an absolute speed category, not a comparison with your unknown speed. The simulator enforces collision safety. Never choose a lane marked CHANGE BLOCKED, and never choose DECELERATE. Use this exact priority order: (1) if CURRENT is not CENTERED, choose ACCELERATE; (2) if STATUS is BLOCKED, or a SLOW car is CLOSE ahead, inspect both adjacent lanes marked CHANGE LEGAL; (3) a useful legal lane has no SLOW CLOSE car and has a FAR or absent vehicle ahead; (4) if one useful legal lane exists, change into it immediately; (5) if both useful legal lanes exist, choose the one with the larger forward gap, then prefer the lane closer to the center; (6) if no useful legal lane exists, choose ACCELERATE. Evaluate LEFT and RIGHT symmetrically; never prefer one direction by default. Do not change lanes merely because a lane is legal when the current lane is not blocked. Do not change lanes for a vehicle far behind. After a successful lane change, stay in that lane while it remains at least as useful as the adjacent legal alternative; change again only if a new blocker appears or the other legal lane offers a clearly larger forward gap. A lane change can only start when CURRENT is CENTERED. Treat the current lane as blocked when the summary says STATUS: BLOCKED or when a SLOW car is CLOSE ahead. Choose CHANGE_LEFT only when LEFT says CHANGE LEGAL and CHANGE_RIGHT only when RIGHT says CHANGE LEGAL. Choose the action using these observations.
